evals.prompt: I have the diamonds dataset at /Users/vnijs/gh/pyrsm/examples/data/data/diamonds.parquet. I want a scatter plot of price (y) versus carat (x), colored by cut, with a linear regression line. Sample to 500 points for readability. Walk me through it.
evals.expected_output: Conversation that: asks for/uses the absolute path, calls scripts/load_data.py, finds and reads diamonds_description.md to confirm price is in dollars, carat is weight, cut is a 5-level quality grade. Identifies the right geom (scatter, since the user wants a point plot of two numerics). Confirms the spec: rsm.eda.visualize(df, x='carat', y='price', geom='scatter', color='cut', smooth='lm', nobs=500, title='Price vs Carat by Cut'). Notes that with smooth='lm' AND color='cut', plotnine fits a SEPARATE linear regression line per cut group (rather than one overall line) — explicitly mentions this useful behavior. Notes the 500-point sample caveat: a 'nobs=500 used' caption will appear; the smoother is fit on the sample, not the full 3000 rows (for a smoother on all data, layer geom_smooth manually). Runs the call and reports the returned object is a plotnine.ggplot — in Jupyter it auto-renders; elsewhere print(p) or p.save('file.png', width=10, height=6, dpi=150). Walks the patterns to look for: positive slope (carat increases price), spread (tight at low carat, wide at high carat — heteroscedasticity), color separation (Ideal cut tends to have lower prices for the same carat — a confound). Optionally recommends layering plotnine extensions if needed: + scale_y_log10() for a log-y view to handle the price skew; + theme_minimal() for a cleaner look; + labs(subtitle='...', caption='Source: pyrsm diamonds') for richer titles.

evals.prompt: Same diamonds data at /Users/vnijs/gh/pyrsm/examples/data/data/diamonds.parquet. After making that scatter plot, I want to extend it with plotnine: (a) use a log y-axis since price is right-skewed, (b) use a minimal theme, (c) add an overall LOESS smoother across all cuts (not per-cut), and (d) save it as a 12×7 inch PNG. Walk me through the plotnine layering.
evals.expected_output: Conversation that: explicitly demonstrates the plotnine extensibility of visualize(). Starts with the base plot from eval 1: p = rsm.eda.visualize(df, x='carat', y='price', geom='scatter', color='cut', smooth='lm', nobs=500). Then layers, IN ORDER: (a) + scale_y_log10() to switch to log price; (b) + theme_minimal() for the theme; (c) + geom_smooth(method='loess', se=False, color='black', linetype='dashed') to add an overall LOESS curve in black (distinct from the per-cut linear smooths in color); (d) p_final.save('price_vs_carat.png', width=12, height=7, dpi=150). Combines into a single chained expression: p_final = (rsm.eda.visualize(...) + scale_y_log10() + theme_minimal() + geom_smooth(method='loess', se=False, color='black', linetype='dashed') + labs(title='Price vs Carat (log y) by Cut', caption='Linear smooth per cut + overall LOESS in dashed black')). Saves and confirms. Names the pattern: 'visualize is the START of the plotnine pipeline. Anything plotnine supports — scales, themes, additional geoms, custom labels — can be added on top.' Reinforces: 'You get pyrsm's polars-friendly conveniences AND the full plotnine API for customization, by composition.' Optionally mentions other extensions the user might find useful (geom_vline at a substantive threshold, scale_color_brewer for a different palette, facet_wrap if comparing too many groups).

evals.prompt: I want a line chart of average diamond price by date, with one line per cut, using /Users/vnijs/gh/pyrsm/examples/data/data/diamonds.parquet. Can I just call rsm.eda.visualize(df, x='date', y='price', geom='line', color='cut')?
evals.expected_output: Conversation that: (1) pushes back on the proposed call — it would NOT give the intended result because the raw data has multiple price observations per date (one per diamond), and geom_line would try to draw a line connecting EVERY observation in row order, producing a jumbled mess; (2) explains: a line chart of 'average price by date by cut' needs the data to be AGGREGATED first to one row per (date, cut) combination; (3) shows the correct workflow: PREPROCESS with polars, THEN visualize. Build the aggregated DataFrame: agg = df.group_by(['date', 'cut']).agg(mean_price=pl.col('price').mean()).sort(['cut', 'date']) — explicitly notes the .sort() is essential because line plots need ordered x; (4) THEN call: rsm.eda.visualize(agg, x='date', y='mean_price', geom='line', color='cut') — explains that visualize auto-groups by color when no explicit group= is set, so each cut gets a continuous connected line; (5) confirms the plot will show 5 lines (one per cut) over the date range (2012-2015), with mean price per (date, cut) on the y-axis; (6) suggests as next steps: layer a smoother (geom_smooth) on top, or use pyrsm-pivot to build the (date, cut) mean table if the user wants a wide-format view for export. (7) Reinforces the broader lesson: 'visualize doesn't aggregate. Get the data into plot-ready shape with polars first (or use a pyrsm.eda function like pivot or explore), then plot.' (8) Optionally also flags that with too many points along the date axis (e.g., if dates were full timestamps), a line chart can become noisy — consider binning to month or quarter first with pl.col('date').dt.truncate('1mo').
